solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unsigned reference books, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: un-signed read as stripped of a sign of the zodiac, here the star sign Aries, so those letters go

parts.note: dictionaries are reference books

explanation.surface: Reference works with no named author, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unsigned' is read as 'without a (star) sign': ARIES leaves DICTIONARIES. The definition 'in a manner of speaking' is literal: diction is a manner of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Diction is a person's way of pronouncing and choosing words, their manner of speaking.

clue.text: Last of summer wine in president's place? Such measures required?

indicators.note: signals that the letters go inside the president's city

parts.note: DC: Washington DC, home of the US president

indicators.note: the final letter of the word summer is taken

parts.note: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Someone mourns the end of summer's wine; desperate measures are called for.
explanation.walkthrough: Last of the Summer Wine was a long-running British TV comedy, which the surface borrows.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are extreme steps taken when matters are desperate, the stock phrase the clue invokes.

clue.text: Female teacher in form

indicators.note: to form is to shape, so the letters of the two words are shaped anew

explanation.surface: A woman teaching in a school class, a form being a British school year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine is a woman's name, so it stands as an example of a female.

clue.text: Piece introduced by popular group

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A new number brought in by a well-liked band.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a piece put into something larger, such as a small map set into a page.

clue.text: Almost the first time one is up late

parts.note: nigh means nearly or almost

indicators.note: the initial letter of the word the is taken

parts.note: bird is slang for a prison term, time served

explanation.surface: Staying up late almost for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRD for prison time comes from rhyming slang (birdlime = time).
explanation.definitionFit: A night bird is a person who habitually stays up late, a night owl.

clue.text: Workers accepting origin of Holy Bible is good

indicators.note: the workers take the other letters inside them

parts.note: worker bees, so workers can be bees

indicators.note: the start of the word Holy gives its first letter

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: Labourers taking up the Bible is a good thing.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave, said of a child, means to act well, to be good.

clue.text: End of knife held by crazy motel owner

indicators.note: the knife's end sits inside the word for crazy

parts.note: bats is informal for mad or crazy

indicators.note: the last letter of the word knife is used

explanation.surface: A madman with a knife runs a motel, a nod to the film Psycho.
explanation.definitionFit: Norman Bates is the knife-wielding motel keeper in Hitchcock's Psycho.

clue.text: Cold shower may reveal his mortal wound

indicators.note: wound as in twisted round, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A cold shower might expose someone's fatal injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' reads as an injury beside 'mortal', but it is the past tense of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall of hail is a shower of ice pellets, so a cold shower is a fair description.

clue.text: Woolly vest's beginning to fit

indicators.note: the start of the word vest gives its first letter

parts.note: an ague is a fit of shivering fever

explanation.surface: A knitted vest begins to fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolly thinking is muddled and imprecise, the sense of vague.

clue.text: True as true, ignoring the odds

parts.note: as and since both mean because

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the second true are dropped, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Something is as true as true, discounting the betting odds.
explanation.definitionFit: True friendship or true feeling is sincere: genuine, honestly meant.

clue.text: Choir members coming into cathedral to sing

indicators.note: the answer comes into, sits within, the run of letters across the words

explanation.surface: Choristers arriving at a cathedral to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: Altos are singers of the part above tenor in a choir.

clue.text: Succeeding as a boarder though no longer young

definitions.meaning: climbing aboard a bus or train

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers progress in life, mounting a vehicle and ageing, three common idioms.

clue.text: Country property has displaced one in this

indicators.note: the property word pushes out a letter and takes its place

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
an estate is landed property

explanation.surface: A rural estate has pushed out a resident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country property' looks like one phrase (a country estate); Country is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for the United States of America, a common informal name for the country.

clue.text: An explorer in conversation, say

indicators.note: say tells us the letters are pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: speak as a noun means talk or jargon, as in office speak

explanation.surface: An explorer chatting, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: John Hanning Speke was the Victorian explorer who found the source of the Nile.

clue.text: Conservative member's ascent

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A Tory MP's rise up the ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb is a rise or upward journey, so it matches ascent.

clue.text: Plan to mingle with obese or skinny people

indicators.note: the letters are mixed together into a new order

explanation.surface: Arranging for fat and thin people to mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Beanpole is slang for a tall thin person, so skinny people.

clue.text: Near Quito, resort with too few people

indicators.note: read as re-sort, sorting the letters again

explanation.surface: A holiday resort near Quito that is short of visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' poses as a holiday spot near Ecuador's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting is inquorate when fewer than the required minimum number attend.

clue.text: Lodge only half visible every few months

parts.note: to quarter is to lodge or house troops

indicators.note: only the latter half of the word only shows

explanation.surface: A lodge that is only partly in view.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarterly means every three months, four times a year.

clue.text: One can spin in fruit machine

indicators.note: the spun letters go inside the fruit

parts.note: an apple is a fruit
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: spinning the letters sets them in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone can spin the reels on a fruit machine, a British slot machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruit machine' is a single phrase on the surface; split it.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance is a device or machine for a household task.

clue.text: Where many Egyptians are ignoring one old queen

indicators.note: the letter for one is left out

parts.note: Alexandria is Egypt's second-largest city
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An old queen who disregards a single subject in Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Alexandra was the wife of Edward VII, a historical British queen.

clue.text: Disconcerted by a hit

parts.note: bashed means struck or hit

explanation.surface: Someone thrown off balance by a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Abashed means embarrassed or put out, the same as disconcerted.

clue.text: Bicycle cleaned half-heartedly

indicators.note: the doubled middle letters are halved, so one goes

parts.note: mopped means cleaned with a mop

explanation.surface: A bike given a lazy wash.
explanation.definitionFit: A moped is a light motorised bicycle with pedals.

clue.text: Stray serving man held up by groom

indicators.note: the soldier is held inside the groom word

parts.note: to groom is to dress, as with hair or a horse

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: a GI is an American serviceman

explanation.surface: A wandering servant is held back by a stable lad.
explanation.definitionFit: To digress is to stray from the main subject.

clue.text: Carry on and take part in heightened drama?

definitions.meaning: act in a play staged higher up

explanation.definitionFit: Children who misbehave are said to carry on, an idiom for playing up.

clue.text: More or less attached to top of tree trunk

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of tree is its first letter

parts.note: or so means approximately

explanation.surface: Approximately attached to the top of a tree trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the body is the torso.

clue.text: Indistinct speech, say, in China

indicators.note: the speaking word is placed within the dynasty

parts.note: Ming is the Chinese dynasty famous for porcelain, fine china
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Unclear talk spoken in China.
explanation.definitionFit: Muttering is low, hard-to-hear speech.

clue.text: German novelist penning old opera

indicators.note: the novelist encloses the letter as a pen holds animals

parts.note: Thomas Mann wrote Death in Venice

explanation.surface: A German author writing an old opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Manon is an opera by Massenet, based on the Abbé Prévost novel.

clue.text: Small and delicate female in river standing up

indicators.note: in a down clue the whole lot is read upwards
the female letter goes inside the river

parts.note: the Nile is the African river

explanation.surface: A dainty woman standing in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin describes someone small and delicate, like an elf.

clue.text: Commiseration not quite right for resolute advocate

indicators.note: the final letter is cut off

parts.note: hard lines is a British expression of sympathy, like bad luck

explanation.surface: Sympathy is not quite the right thing for a staunch campaigner.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardliner sticks uncompromisingly to a firm policy, a resolute supporter.

clue.text: Guard criminal

explanation.definitionFit: A fence both guards land as a barrier and, in slang, deals in stolen goods.

clue.text: Calls to be a reformed character?

definitions.meaning: giving up wrongdoing, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: To drop in is to call on someone unannounced; split, it means to abandon sin.

clue.text: City in 11 taking a long time to accept British leading lady

indicators.note: the long-time word takes in the queen's letters

parts.note: yonks is British slang for ages
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the British queen

explanation.surface: A town where a long run takes on a British star actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonkers is a city in New York State, in the USA.
